summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 7% to ₹160 crore while PAT fell 55% to ₹3.67 crore; management targets ₹60 crore from Malur in FY27.
summary.overview: Management admitted missing its FY26 sales target, blaming delayed commissioning of Malur machinery and a workforce readiness gap. EBITDA margin slipped to 8.7% from 9.1%, and PAT fell 55% YoY to ₹3.67 crore. Management says Malur is now fully operational, the paint shop phase one went live in June 2026, and shipments to the largest customer have started. Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 8–11% and a ~20% revenue CAGR over three years. Analysts pressed on plant utilisation, idle capacity, cost structure and the gap between guidance and a 13–14% margin ambition.

segments.name: Construction equipment fabrication
segments.commentary: About 53% of FY26 revenue; management says customer capacity expansion is driving demand, and Malur was built for large, complex assemblies.

segments.name: Malur plant (Bangalore new facility)
segments.commentary: Management targets ~₹60 crore revenue in FY27 (analyst pencilled ₹50-60 crore), rising to ₹100 crore by FY29; ~₹25-30 crore of existing Bangalore business is being shifted there.

segments.name: Pune plant
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36-38 crore in FY26; management targets at least ₹50 crore in FY27 (~80% utilisation), excluding new export trial orders.

segments.name: Vadodara plant
segments.commentary: Management sees flat volumes as a major customer's business declined; first small US export orders received recently.

segments.name: Power / electrical
segments.commentary: Largest electrical customer Schneider's offtake fell sharply from Q4 FY25; management sees little benefit from the power sector boom to its current customer mix.

segments.name: Robotics / automation
segments.commentary: FY26 business about ₹2 crore; inquiries up 300-400% since March; FY27 target ₹5-10 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Malur revenue ~₹60 crore; ₹100 crore by FY29, possibly earlier.
Overall revenue CAGR ~20% over next three years; FY26 base is ₹160 crore, and analysts cited ~₹190 crore as a plausible FY27 level.
EBITDA margin band 8-11%; management says it agrees double-digit EBITDA is needed and is aiming for it, but gave no 13-14% target.
Caterpillar business expected to grow at least 15-20% in FY27; management says talks are very positive.
Employee cost to be a key challenge, with Karnataka minimum wage hikes of up to 30% flagged; the goal is for employee cost as a percentage of sales to fall below FY26 levels.
Finance cost expected to stay around Q4 FY26 level; second paint shop phase capex ~₹2-3 crore still pending.
risks_watch: Execution risk: management admitted FY26 target miss; the Malur ramp-up depends on the largest customer's volumes.
Schneider (power switchgear) offtake decline from Q4 FY25 with no clear explanation.
Employee cost inflation, especially Karnataka minimum wage increases of up to 30%.
Overlap between Malur and Bangalore revenue means the net growth from Malur is ₹30-35 crore, not ₹60 crore.
Vadodara utilisation weak; Pune utilisation dependent on new export customers.
Freight cost and geopolitical or raw material volatility; pass-through lag of one quarter.
Lack of a quantified margin path beyond 8-11%; analyst pressure for 13-14%.
summary.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on FY26 execution, with management owning the miss; guidance is described as conservative, and the outlook for FY27 is cautiously optimistic. On margins and idle capacity, management was less specific and somewhat defensive when pressed by analysts.
key_quotes: As the company's MD, I take full responsibility for this shortfall.
We are still climbing the learning curve; we have n't climbed it.
So I think based on that , if we keep on , if we increase 20 -25% compounded as w e have been talking about, definitely a good part of that should flow downwards as EBITDA.
And if we don't do that, I would also treat it as a failure.

financial_highlights.change: stable over last three years per management

qa_highlights.question: Dhwanil Desai asked what FY27 Malur revenue to expect, whether product approvals are in place, and whether ₹50-60 crore is incremental to ₹160 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ₹60 crore from Malur in FY27 and ₹100 crore by FY29, with product approvals in place and shipments started to the largest customer. About ₹25-30 crore of the ₹160 crore base will move from Bommasandra to Malur, so the addition is not simply ₹160 + ₹60.

qa_highlights.question: Dhwanil Desai asked whether the margin path could move from 8-9% toward 13-15% as Malur utilisation ramps.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an EBITDA band of 8-11% for FY27 and declined to quantify beyond that. Harshad Patel said gross margin has held for three years and a good part of 20-25% compounded growth should flow to EBITDA, aided by automation.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta questioned why the company keeps adding plants while Pune and Vadodara run at low utilisation and whether consolidation is planned.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new Bangalore plant was needed because the old facility lacked space for Caterpillar growth, and no other new plants are planned. Harshad Patel said Pune will reach about 80% utilisation and that idle plants must improve or be closed, while citing skill and certification differences across plants.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mehta asked whether FY27 revenue should be closer to ₹190 crore or ₹210-225 crore, and how raw material price increases are passed through.
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Agrawal said the outlook is conservative given geopolitical and raw material volatility, while agreeing the projections could make the higher number achievable. Pass-through is quarterly when prices move more than ±5%, with a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Jain asked about Caterpillar growth and the power sector opportunity.
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Agrawal said Caterpillar talks are very positive, with at least 15-20% growth expected in FY27. Harshad Patel said power sector gains are mainly in transformers and not in the company's switchgear customers, and Schneider offtake fell sharply with no explanation.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Jain asked about Pune revenue potential, export margins and robotics targets, and employee cost trajectory.
qa_highlights.answer: Harshad Patel targets at least ₹50 crore from Pune in FY27 (from ₹36 crore) and robotics ₹5-10 crore. On employee cost, he said Karnataka wage rises of up to 30% are a major challenge and the target is employee cost as a % of sales below FY26, with the labour line affected by duplication across old and new plants last year.

qa_highlights.question: Manoj Dua asked how to reach 13-14% EBITDA margin in the long term and what the path is beyond ₹300 crore revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Harshad Patel agreed double-digit EBITDA is needed and said the company must aim for it, calling a failure to do so a failure. On growth beyond ₹300 crore, he said global earthmoving export demand is the focus and tube business is on hold for the next 12 months.

capex_capacity: Malur plant is fully operational per management; tooling for target product mix (medium and heavy fabrication for construction equipment) is in place and validated.
Phase one of in-house paint shop went operational in June 2026; second paint shop phase still pending with ~₹2-3 crore capex.

Malur FY27 revenue target ~₹60 crore; ₹100 crore by FY29, possibly before FY29. Approximately ₹25-30 crore of the existing Bangalore (Bommasandra) business is shifted to Malur, so net incremental is smaller.

Pune plant: FY26 revenue ~₹36-38 crore; management targets at least ₹50 crore in FY27 (~80% utilisation), with full capacity possibly by Q3 FY27; excludes new export trial orders from two or three MNCs.
Vadodara: flat outlook as a major customer's business declined; first small US export orders received recently.
Robotics: ~5-6 robots installed so far; another 8-10 planned across facilities this year.
Management said no new plants set up in last three years apart from Malur and none currently planned; tube business put on hold for next 12 months.
demand_pricing: Caterpillar: talks described as very positive; management expects at least 15-20% growth in FY27 and sees Caterpillar's engine division (Perkins, Hosur) as a possible new inquiry source.

Power/electrical: Schneider offtake fell sharply from Q4 FY25 with no explanation given; management sees little benefit from power sector boom for current switchgear customer mix (Schneider, ABB, Siemens).
Robotics: FY26 business ~₹2 crore; inquiries up 300-400% since March; FY27 target ₹5 crore, possibly revised to ₹10 crore if pipeline converts by June-July.
Exports: FY26 ₹22.83 crore (14.2% of revenue); management says margins on export should stay above domestic, with more complex export work earning higher margins.
Pricing: quarterly raw material pass-through to majority of customers when prices move more than ±5%, with about one-quarter lag.
Employee cost: Karnataka minimum wage hikes of up to 30% flagged as a key challenge; management targets lower employee cost as % of sales than FY26.

adds.what: Malur (Bangalore) new facility, fully operational per management; targets ~₹60 crore FY27 revenue
In-house paint shop phase one (went live June 2026); second phase pending
Robotics: ~5-6 robots installed; another 8-10 planned this year
Pune plant ramp to at least ₹50 crore FY27 (~80% utilisation), full capacity possibly by Q3 FY27

growth.why: Management guides ~20% revenue CAGR over three years and Malur ₹60 crore plus Pune ₹50 crore for FY27, backed by the commissioned Malur plant, Pune ramp to ~80% utilisation and Caterpillar talks, but the brief gives no firm order book figures and Schneider volumes are falling, so backing is partial.
